sources.entry: logging - (Python standard library) Logging facility for Python.

summary.name: logging
summary.one_liner: Python's standard library module for flexible event logging in applications and libraries, documented here as an API reference.
use_cases: Writing application logs to a file
Adding logging to a Python library without configuring output
Including custom fields in log messages
Debugging with stack traces in log output
Routing log messages to multiple destinations
summary.what_it_does: The page is the API reference for Python's logging module. It documents the Logger class (getLogger, setLevel, propagation to ancestor loggers, filters, and handlers), the standard numeric log levels from DEBUG (10) to CRITICAL (50), and the Handler and Formatter base classes. It shows the idiomatic pattern of creating a module-level logger with getLogger(__name__) and configuring only the root logger with basicConfig(). It also explains keyword options such as exc_info, stack_info, stacklevel and extra for individual log calls.
notable: Hierarchical loggers named by module via getLogger(__name__) with propagation to the root logger
Standard numeric levels plus the ability to define custom levels
extra keyword adds custom attributes to log records for use in formatters
caveats: The page is API reference only; it points to separate tutorials for basic and advanced usage
Formatters using custom extra fields will fail to log if the expected keys are missing from extra
The obsolete warn method is deprecated in favor of warning
